title: Case study and sub-issue plan for competitor parity in natural-language math (#227)
body:
Closes #227

## Summary

Deep case study of how far this calculator is from "every competitor plus scientific prose in any language", with executable corpora, an automated gap checker, and the full work plan filed as 18 sub-issues (#229 to #246) with GitHub blocker dependencies.

- `scripts/competitor-coverage.mjs` runs every corpus row through the one-shot CLI and classifies it as `supported`, `different`, `unsupported` or `timeout`; writes `results/coverage-report.md` and a compact `coverage-baseline.json`; `--baseline` fails on regressions. Unit-tested by `scripts/competitor-coverage.test.mjs` (runs in the existing `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` CI step).
- `scripts/import-competitor-corpus.mjs` extracts single-expression assertions from the fend, libqalculate, Numbat, Rink and math.js test suites (2550 rows, upstream licenses cited in the file header).
- `docs/case-studies/issue-227/`: README with requirement inventory, method, measurements, error classes, solution options, component evaluation and dependency graph; `competitor-inventory.md`; `natural-language-corpus.md`; three corpora (3055 rows); the generated report and baseline; the 18 sub-issue bodies exactly as filed plus `issues.json`.

## Measured state (v0.22.0, 3055 rows, 24 s)

| Source | Rows | Supported | Different | Unsupported |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| fend | 1098 | 33.6% | 67 | 662 |
| Qalculate! | 656 | 9.3% | 14 | 581 |
| math.js | 297 | 26.9% | 22 | 195 |
| Numbat | 289 | 22.5% | 22 | 202 |
| Rink | 210 | 0.0% | 33 | 177 |
| Soulver docs | 266 | 9.4% | 32 | 209 |
| Numi, Wolfram\|Alpha, Google, Calca, Raycast, Apple, Frink | 77 | 39.0% | 3 | 44 |
| Scientific quotes in 13 languages | 162 | 6.2% | 20 | 132 |
| **All** | **3055** | **20.9%** | **213** | **2202** |

Most important finding: 213 rows return a silently wrong number, for example `3,000 minus 12` gives `-9`, `200 + 10%` gives `200.1`, `10m × 10m` gives `0.0001`, `3 squared plus 4 squared` gives `7 squared`, `5pm - 7pm` gives `-2 hours`, `0xff` gives `0 XFF`.

All are attached as sub-issues of #227 through the sub-issues API; the 37 blocker edges are registered through the issue-dependencies API (`experiments/issue-227/create-sub-issues.mjs`, idempotent).

## How to reproduce

```sh
cargo build --release --bin link-calculator
node scripts/competitor-coverage.mjs --baseline docs/case-studies/issue-227/results/coverage-baseline.json
node --test scripts/*.test.mjs
```

The runner prints the per-source table and `No regressions against …`; the full row-level report is regenerated at `docs/case-studies/issue-227/results/coverage-report.md`.

## Notes

- No Rust code changes; `cargo fmt --check`, `node scripts/check-file-size.mjs` and the script tests pass locally.
- `coverage-results.json` (1 MB, full row output) is gitignored; the committed baseline is the compact per-row status.
- Upstream test data is used as an executable reference under the quoted licenses and is not relicensed.
- Assumptions are listed at the end of the case-study README (how "beat exactly" is measured, live-data rows only have to evaluate, conflicting competitor conventions are resolved per sub-issue).
- The 18 sub-issues (#229 to #246) are the work plan filed by this PR; they stay open after merge and are not closed by it. Only #227 is closed here.
- Web dependencies are bumped to their latest releases (vite, @vitejs/plugin-react, jsdom, react-i18next, links-notation, lino-objects-codec, browser-commander) because the Dependency Freshness job fails on any release published after `main` last passed; the 229 web unit tests and `tsc` pass with the new versions.
